q1: SELECT NAME FROM SALESPERSON AS S WHERE 0 = ( SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ORDERS AS O JOIN COMPANY AS C ON O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID WHERE O.SALES_ID = S.SALES_ID AND C.NAME = 'RED' )
q2: WITH TEMP AS ( SELECT S.NAME, SUM(CASE WHEN C.NAME = 'RED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS HAS_RED FROM SALESPERSON S LEFT JOIN ORDERS O ON S.SALES_ID = O.SALES_ID LEFT JOIN COMPANY C ON O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID GROUP BY S.NAME ) SELECT NAME FROM TEMP WHERE HAS_RED = 0
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT NAME FROM SALESPERSON AS S WHERE 0 = ( SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ORDERS AS O JOIN COMPANY AS C ON O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID WHERE O.SALES_ID = S.SALES_ID AND C.NAME = 'RED' )
q2_prompt_sql: WITH TEMP AS ( SELECT S.NAME, SUM(CASE WHEN C.NAME = 'RED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS HAS_RED FROM SALESPERSON S LEFT JOIN ORDERS O ON S.SALES_ID = O.SALES_ID LEFT JOIN COMPANY C ON O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID GROUP BY S.NAME ) SELECT NAME FROM TEMP WHERE HAS_RED = 0
explanation: Both queries aim to identify salespersons who have not made any orders for the company named 'RED'. The logic in both queries is equivalent, as they both use subqueries or CTEs to count the number of orders for 'RED' and filter out salespersons with no such orders.
